Use Letterman in your browser

Or use Letterman in your browser. No download.

Windows will warn you. Here are the clicks.

Letterman is free, and this first version is not signed with a paid certificate. Windows, and sometimes your browser, warns about any new file like that. The warning is about the file being new. It is not a finding that anything is wrong.

What Windows says:

Windows protected your PC. Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognized app from starting. Running this app might put your PC at risk.

  1. Keep. Your browser may ask whether to keep the file. Choose Keep.
  2. More info. Open the file. If Windows shows the warning above, click More info.
  3. Check the file name, then Run anyway. Under More info, the app name should read Letterman-Setup.exe. If it does, click Run anyway.
  4. It installs and opens. Letterman installs in a few seconds and opens by itself. After that you will find it in the Start menu.

If the name is different, do not run it. Anything other than Letterman-Setup.exe is not from this page. Close the window and download again from here.

If there is no Run anyway button, your PC is using Smart App Control, which only allows signed apps. Use Letterman in your browser instead, and do not turn Smart App Control off.

For advanced users

Letterman installs for you only. It needs no administrator rights. It updates itself quietly from the public repository's releases, and it never restarts without asking you.

Fingerprints (SHA-256)

Each release lists its fingerprints here.

To check a download, run Get-FileHash .\Letterman-Setup.exe in PowerShell and compare the result. The spaces above are only for reading; ignore them when you compare.

To uninstall

Open Windows Settings, then Apps, then Installed apps. Find Letterman and choose Uninstall. Your answers are kept in Letterman's own data folder until you erase them in the app, under Your data.
